title: UK endorsed 44 recommendations for AI healthcare regulation
source_used: Digital Watch Observatory (relaying UK government and MHRA announcement)
key_facts: The UK government accepted all 44 recommendations of the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare; its response was published on 6 October 2026.
The response sets initial next steps for each recommendation and ten priority areas; a programme board will oversee delivery and a full roadmap is due by spring 2027.
The MHRA set up the commission in September 2025; it published its recommendations on 10 September 2026 after gathering evidence from more than 12,000 people.
Central idea: AI medical devices should be assessed and monitored through their working life, not mainly once before sale.
The MHRA opened applications for phase 3 of AI Airlock, a sandbox for AI medical devices, with three more years of government funding; first participants are chosen in November 2026.
Draft guidance is due by December 2026; commitments include informing patients about AI in their care and access to redress.
quote_evidence: The UK government has accepted all 44 recommendations set out by the National Commission into the Regulation of AI in Healthcare (Commission).
Detailed measures are still to be developed, with draft guidance due by December 2026 and an implementation roadmap by spring 2027.
why_it_matters_hint: Shifts UK medical-AI oversight to continuous monitoring after launch.
notes: Government response published 6 Oct, before the 8 Oct window, so score lowered by 1.
